title: Delegated sign-off, expiry windows, and auditable trails for progressive model rollouts
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem statement: As Redwood expands automated canary/A-B/shadow rollouts and auto-rollback capabilities, operators need a flexible, auditable approval system that balances speed with governance. Current manual sign-off flows are slow for low-risk changes, but we lack safe delegation, expiry/TTL semantics on approvals, and explicit audit metadata linked to telemetry and rollback triggers.

Goal: Design and ship a Delegated Approval Framework that: 1) supports role-based approvals (approver, reviewer, emergency-rollback), 2) allows delegation rules with thresholds (e.g., product owners can approve up to X% traffic, safety owners required above Y%), 3) attaches structured audit metadata to every rollout and automated rollback, 4) includes approval expiry (time-to-live) and automatic re-approval triggers if a rollout is paused or extended, and 5) integrates with Console dashboards and incident timelines for end-to-end traceability.

Scope: UX and API for creating approval policies, enforcement in the control plane for canary/A-B/shadow traffic, audit log schema and retention, and guardrails for auto-rollback events. Out of scope for this ticket: long-term archival policies for audit blobs (handled by Compliance team) and RBAC sync with external IdP (separate integration ticket).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Console UI to create delegated approval policies with role thresholds and TTLs.
- API endpoints for evaluating whether a rollout can progress and for recording approvals (with metadata: approver id, role, TTL, rationale, linked PR/PR-ID).
- Enforced checks in rollout orchestration: block progression if required approvals are missing or expired.
- Automatic re-request flow: if approval TTL expires mid-rollout, orchestration pauses and notifies stakeholders.
- Full audit row emitted for each rollout event (rollout start, step change, approval granted/expired, rollback start, rollback reason) with links to telemetry snapshot and the triggering metric.
- Playbook for emergency rollback that allows a short-lived emergency approver role to bypass delegation but leaves a tamper-evident audit trail.

Operational trade-offs considered: Blocking on too many required sign-offs increases time-to-value; permitting too much delegation increases risk. We propose a hybrid default policy that allows up to 20% traffic by a single product approver; any rollout exceeding 20% or touching datasets labeled "sensitive" requires two approvers: an ML owner and a Security compliance reviewer. TTL default is 72 hours.
